clips.text_zh: 全球都跌，印尼、印度、法國、意大利齊冧。連Mamdani都搞到啲business走晒去Texas。anons話hashest time先係我哋嘅time。咁我而家應該short咩？prop firm個account又見紅，CFD margin叫緊。CFD又輸多一鑊，今個月學費又交多一次。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Everything is falling apart right now. Another Indonesian anon says his country's stock crash is the worst in history. France and Italy are also falling. The US might not drop as sharply because, ironically, Mamdani pushed businesses from New York to Texas. This is not blackpilling. The post reminds anons that we strive in the harshest times. So when do you short?
clips.text_en_b2: Markets are unraveling across the board right now, with Indonesia, India, France, and Italy all taking heavy hits in unison. One Indonesian poster claims his country's crash is the worst in recorded history, while Mamdani's policies have pushed firms out of New York toward Texas. Anons keep insisting the harshest conditions bring out the best returns, so timing matters. My prop firm account keeps bleeding red, CFD margin calls keep piling up, and I have lost my CFD track entirely.🙏
clips.text_en_c1: Markets across virtually every region appear to be capitulating simultaneously, with Indonesia, India, France, and Italy all posting steep declines on heavy volume. One Indonesian poster describes his domestic crash as historically severe, while Mamdani's New York policies have paradoxically redirected capital toward Texas, cushioning the US from the worst of the selloff. This is not blackpilling. Veterans remind the thread that those who position themselves correctly during periods of maximum stress are those who ultimately benefit. Given that prop firm accounts remain deep in the red and CFD margin calls continue stacking up, the pressing question remains: what instruments should one actually be shorting right now?
clips.text_en_c2: Global equity markets are presently in freefall, with Indonesia, India, France, and Italy all posting precipitous declines. An Indonesian poster describes his domestic crash as the gravest in living memory. The United States, paradoxically, may weather the storm with less severity: Mamdani's policies have, by his own account, driven a substantial migration of capital and businesses from New York toward Texas. The thread is emphatically not a blackpill exercise; rather, it reminds participants that the harshest macroeconomic conditions historically have been the moments when the contrarian mind is most amply rewarded. The practical question, then, is how one should structure short exposure right now. Prop-firm accounts bleed, CFD margins issue their customary margin calls, and tuition fees, paid monthly to the market's school of hard knocks, accumulate yet again. Timing, in such environments, is everything.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread about timing a global short as markets dump.

clips.text_zh: TSLA earnings又到，Elon今次講Optimus同FSD嘅progress。SpaceX Starship test緊，Starlink收入又係亮點。我成日睇X platform嗰邊搞事，唔知今次條tweet會唔會又推動個股。CFD倉未開，等緊direction。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Tesla earnings season is open and anons are watching the new delivery numbers and any Optimus or FSD update from Elon. SpaceX is also testing Starship again, and Starlink revenue keeps growing. The big question is which Musk tweet or shitpost moves TSLA after the print. Add Nvidia and the AI chip story on top.
clips.text_en_b2: Tesla earnings season has kicked off and anons are glued to fresh delivery figures alongside any Optimus or FSD progress Musk might announce. SpaceX is putting Starship through fresh trials while Starlink revenue remains the standout performer in the portfolio. The million-dollar question is which Musk tweet or shitpost will send TSLA flying after the print, given his track record of moving markets. Nvidia and the AI chip narrative still hang over everything. My CFD position is still flat, waiting for clear direction.🙏
clips.text_en_c1: Tesla's earnings cycle has formally commenced, and anons are poring over the freshly released delivery figures alongside any commentary Musk offers regarding Optimus and FSD progress. SpaceX continues iterating on Starship prototypes, while Starlink revenue growth remains a consistent standout in the broader narrative. The recurring uncertainty, as ever, is whether a single post on X will materially shift TSLA's direction immediately following the print, given how heavily the stock responds to Musk's whims. Layer Nvidia's ongoing AI chip saga on top of all of this, and the open question is which catalysts will dominate sentiment in the sessions ahead.
clips.text_en_c2: Tesla's quarterly earnings cycle has commenced, and the customary circus of analyst speculation has resumed in earnest. Elon Musk is expected to deliver updates on Optimus and Full Self-Driving, the two product narratives that increasingly define the company's valuation. Meanwhile, SpaceX continues iterative testing of Starship, and Starlink revenue has emerged as the quietly compounding line item that keeps institutional interest piqued. The more intriguing variable, however, remains Musk's X account: a single ill-considered tweet or facetious shitpost has, on numerous prior occasions, propelled TSLA in directions no earnings model could have anticipated. Against this backdrop, Nvidia and the broader AI-chip narrative exert an undeniable gravitational pull on the stock. Speculative CFD positioning remains uncommitted, pending clarification of directional intent. Pray.
clips.source_hint: Synth-Musk fallback using the IDX thread slot for TSLA/SpaceX coverage.

clips.text_zh: 印尼stock market crash得最勁，MSCI踢咗佢哋出emerging market。一個國家可以跌到咁，背後一定係governance同soil嗰邊都出晒事。我做GI report成日諗，factor of safety唔夠，再加sub-80IQ management，地基都會冧。廢柴國家真係睇唔過。
clips.text_en_b1: The Indonesian stock market just died. It is the worst crash in the history of the Indonesian market after a year-long bear run. MSCI just kicked Indonesia out of emerging markets. The country is officially standalone, managed by extreme corruption and voted in by a low-IQ population. The op says it is hopeless and his future is dead too.
clips.text_en_b2: The Indonesian stock market has effectively collapsed, registering the worst single crash in its history following a brutal year-long bear run. MSCI has now downgraded Indonesia out of emerging market status, leaving the country stranded as a standalone jurisdiction. The original poster lays the blame squarely on systemic corruption and a sub-80 IQ electorate that keeps voting in the same broken establishment. He concludes the situation is utterly hopeless, adding that his own future feels just as dead as the index.
clips.text_en_c1: Indonesia's equity market has effectively collapsed, registering what anons describe as the most severe downturn in its recorded history following a year-long sustained bear phase. MSCI's decision to formally reclassify Indonesia out of emerging market indices has left the country stranded as a standalone jurisdiction, compounding an already grim outlook. The post attributes the rout to entrenched governance failures compounded by what it characterizes as a substantially sub-average electorate that has tolerated systemic corruption for decades. Beyond the macroeconomic implications, the op appears personally devastated, suggesting that any prospect of meaningful recovery, whether professional or national, has effectively evaporated.
clips.text_en_c2: The Indonesian stock exchange has effectively ceased to function as a viable investment vehicle, having endured what its own citizens describe as the most catastrophic crash in the nation's recorded market history, perpetrated against the backdrop of a year-long secular bear trend. MSCI's decision to eject Indonesia from its emerging-market indices crystallises the institutional verdict: the country now stands alone, bereft of the foreign capital flows such classification confers. Beneath the surface, the diagnosis is depressingly familiar to anyone versed in soil mechanics or structural engineering: factor of safety is catastrophically inadequate, foundation conditions have failed, and the load-bearing elements of governance are compromised beyond remediation. The sub-eighty-IQ electorate, having installed yet another cohort of kleptocratic managers, has engineered precisely the outcome their competence predicted.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ OP ranting about Indonesia losing MSCI emerging market status after a historic drop.

clips.text_zh: 有anon話manual laborers就嚟被robots取代，訓練佢哋做地盤嗰啲physical task原來好easy。我做slope survey同soil nailing都諗，Optimus同Boston Dynamics咁落嚟，wireless inspection、rebar tie、drone survey全部自動化。Engineer嘅value最後係load path同judgment，唔係落手落腳。😭
clips.text_en_b1: A biz poster says he wishes he could warn manual laborers how fucked they are. Training robots to do physical tasks turned out to be surprisingly easy, citing an X post about AI-driven robotics progress. It is not just white-collar anymore. Blue-collar site work, lifting, and repetitive tasks are the first ones to go, and that hits construction directly.
clips.text_en_b2: A biz poster wishes he could warn manual laborers just how screwed they really are, because training robots to handle physical site tasks has turned out to be far easier than anyone anticipated. He cites an X post showing rapid AI-driven robotics progress, noting the threat is no longer confined to white-collar desks. Blue-collar construction work, heavy lifting, and repetitive tasks are the obvious first casualties, and that reality hits the building industry head-on. Engineers should probably start bracing for impact now.😭
clips.text_en_c1: A biz regular laments that manual laborers remain dangerously oblivious to the scale of disruption bearing down on them, as recent demonstrations have shown that training robots to execute physical site tasks is far less daunting than previously assumed. The implications extend well beyond white-collar displacement; rebar tying, drone surveying, slope inspection, and other repetitive construction workflows are squarely within reach of platforms such as Optimus and Boston Dynamics. For those in geotechnical disciplines, this shift is particularly stark. The residual value of trained engineers will inevitably reside in judgment, load path reasoning, and design accountability rather than in hands-on execution on site.
clips.text_en_c2: A correspondent on the business board articulates a sentiment he wishes to impart to every manual labourer before the reckoning arrives: the displacement event is no longer a distant hypothetical. Training robots to execute physical tasks, once deemed the intractable frontier of automation, has proven surprisingly tractable, as evidenced by recent demonstrations catalogued across X. The industry-wide implications extend well beyond white-collar professional services; indeed, it is the blue-collar trades, the unglamorous repetitive labour of construction sites, that appear destined for obsolescence first. Rebar tying, drone-enabled surveying, wireless inspection, slope monitoring, soil nailing, all manner of rudimentary site competencies have become trivially automatable. What ultimately survives, if anything does, is the engineer's cultivated capacity for judgement, for synthesising load paths and failure modes that no embodied intelligence can yet replicate. Tears are shed.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread arguing robots are coming for manual labor faster than expected.

clips.text_zh: /g/ 講AI真係食晒programmer，vibecoding加layoff加freeze hiring，code monkey個bubble爆。我唔係programmer但我睇到trend，software都中招，civil engineering都要識下AI tool先唔會被淘汰。考FE嗰陣coding section都加咗。靠AI續命ok，但唔好成世靠。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: How does /g/ feel about AI really replacing software engineers now that the dust has settled? With vibe coding, mass layoffs, and no hiring, the post says it is funny that codemonkeys thought AI would only hit truckers, artists, or useless eaters, but never programming. The lesson: only more jobs, never fewer, turned out to be cope.
clips.text_en_b2: How is /g/ processing the fact that AI has genuinely eaten software engineers now that the initial hype has worn off? With vibe coding flooding the market, mass layoffs rolling through the industry, and a total freeze on hiring, the poster finds it hilarious that codemonkeys convinced themselves AI would only displace truckers, artists, or so-called useless eaters. Nobody seriously believed programming itself was on the chopping block, yet here we are.
clips.text_en_c1: With sufficient hindsight now accumulated, the prevailing sentiment on /g/ is that artificial intelligence has unequivocally displaced software engineers in ways that nobody anticipated on this scale. The convergence of vibe coding tools, mass industry layoffs, and a prolonged hiring freeze has effectively burst the bubble in which codemonkeys had insulated themselves. It is, the poster wryly notes, rather remarkable how confident programmers were that automation would eliminate truckers, illustrators, or other vulnerable groups, yet somehow spare their own profession indefinitely. The hard lesson reinforced across the thread is that 'more jobs created' narratives consistently function as cope rather than credible economic forecasting.
clips.text_en_c2: Now that the initial euphoria has subsided and the structural consequences have clarified, the prevailing sentiment on the technology board is that AI has, incontrovertibly, commenced the systematic displacement of software engineers. The contributory forces are well-rehearsed: vibe coding has collapsed the entry barrier to functional output, mass layoffs continue apace, and hiring freezes have calcified into permanent policy. What renders the situation especially piquant is that the codemonkey class, having long assumed itself immune to automation, derided earlier predictions by noting that AI would surely consume only truckers, artists, and the so-called useless eaters, never the exalted programmer. Such hubris, the original poster observes, now stands exposed as cope of the most florid variety. The broader lesson, applicable even to civil engineers evaluating FE examinations, is that automation从来不只削减岗位, it transmutes them entirely. Adapt accordingly.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread debating whether AI has finally killed coding as a career.

clips.text_zh: 美國終於起返Hong Kong式嘅dense apartment，100 Gold Street project下城落實，1,250呎高嘅tower有4,000幾個family-size unit，30,000呎地住20,000人，density勁過我哋MK。NYC搞成咁，係咪證明dense living先係future？我就唔太buy，我嫌太焗。
clips.text_en_b1: The US will finally start getting dense, Hong Kong-style apartment buildings. The '100 Gold Street' development has been approved for Lower Manhattan. The project includes a 1,250-foot apartment tower with more than 4,000 family-sized residential units. Around 20,000 people could live on about 30,000 square feet, making it the densest residential block in America.
clips.text_en_b2: America is finally set to get dense, Hong Kong-style apartment developments, with the 100 Gold Street project officially approved for Lower Manhattan. The plan features a 1,250-foot residential tower packing in more than 4,000 family-sized units, potentially housing roughly 20,000 residents on a footprint of around 30,000 square feet. That density would make it the most packed residential block in the entire country, easily surpassing anything currently standing. The poster remains skeptical, though, calling the whole idea far too claustrophobic to actually live in.
clips.text_en_c1: America appears poised to belatedly embrace the kind of high-density residential architecture that has long defined Hong Kong, with the recently greenlit 100 Gold Street development in Lower Manhattan serving as the flagship example. The project envisions a 1,250-foot tower containing in excess of 4,000 family-sized units, potentially housing roughly 20,000 residents across a footprint of merely 30,000 square feet, a density figure that would render it the most concentrated residential block anywhere in the United States. Should such developments proliferate, the question becomes whether dense, vertically integrated living truly constitutes the inevitable urban future, or merely an ideologically driven overcorrection to decades of suburban sprawl.
clips.text_en_c2: Lower Manhattan is poised to receive its inaugural Hong Kong-caliber residential tower, marking the moment America finally internalises the architectural logic of vertical density. The recently sanctioned 100 Gold Street development envisages a 1,250-foot structure housing upwards of four thousand family-sized units, with projected occupancy approaching twenty thousand residents compressed onto a footprint of merely thirty thousand square feet. Such figures dwarf even the celebrated density of Mong Kok, rendering the project statistically the most concentrated residential enclave in the United States. Whether this presages a broader American embrace of high-rise living, or merely constitutes an isolated concession to a constrained parcel, remains genuinely contested. The original poster, for his part, confesses to finding such arrangements visually oppressive and acoustically suffocating, declining to be persuaded that claustrophobic proximity constitutes the future of urban habitation.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ thread on New York approving a Hong Kong-density residential tower.

clips.text_zh: /fit/ 問keto diet一邊burn fat一邊build muscle得唔得，話protein synthesis要carbs。我自己gym routine成日cut又cut唔到body fat，仲要見肥仔信日日gym晒post都唔好意思。去gym之前食杯hot cocoa都算pre-workout啦lol。
clips.text_en_b1: A fit anon asks if keto gains are legit. Can you build muscle and burn fat at the same time in ketosis? He says he has done keto a few times and successfully lost body fat each time, but never tested it for muscle. The post asks if carbs are really required for protein synthesis beyond a small net amount per day.
clips.text_en_b2: A fit anon is asking whether keto gains are genuinely legit, wondering if you can realistically build muscle and burn fat simultaneously while staying in deep ketosis. He mentions running keto cycles repeatedly and successfully stripping body fat each time, although he never seriously tested it for muscle retention. The core question is whether carbs are truly necessary for protein synthesis beyond a modest daily net amount. He confesses he feels embarrassed posting gym updates now.
clips.text_en_c1: A /fit/ regular poses the perennial question of whether genuine hypertrophy can coexist with sustained fat oxidation under a ketogenic framework, given that protein synthesis is conventionally understood to require a minimum carbohydrate substrate. He reports having cycled through keto on multiple occasions and achieved consistent fat loss each time, yet concedes he has never rigorously evaluated its effects on lean mass accrual. The thread debates whether the carbohydrate threshold for anabolic function is genuinely substantial or merely nominal per diem, with respondents split between those citing clinical literature and gym-floor empiricists who argue practical outcomes largely diverge from textbook physiology.
clips.text_en_c2: A fitness board participant raises the perennial question of whether ketogenic dieting permits concurrent fat oxidation and myofibrillar hypertrophy, noting that prevailing biochemistry holds carbohydrate intake indispensable for maximal protein synthesis. He recounts repeated forays into nutritional ketosis during which adipose tissue was dutifully shed, yet concedes he never subjected the protocol to a rigorous muscular development trial. The underlying biological dispute concerns threshold effects: proponents argue a modest daily net carbohydrate allotment suffices to drive leucine-mediated translation, whereas adherents of stricter macros insist otherwise. He confesses his own recomp cut has stalled interminably, notwithstanding conscientious gym attendance, whilst observing certain overweight acquaintances who persist in posting subpar workout content. Until peer-reviewed consensus crystallises, his pre-lifting ritual of consuming a mug of hot cocoa shall serve, however unorthodox, as adequate preparation.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ thread asking whether lifting on keto actually builds muscle.

clips.text_zh: /a/ 有storytime開緊亂馬1/2 manga，配合新一季anime，chapter 92-94。我細個睇TVB播過，呢套嘢真係classic。今日做完GI report返嚟，沖杯咖啡慢慢睇。Gundam 00嗰套我反而想re-watch多次。
clips.text_en_b1: An anon is storytiming the Ranma 1/2 manga alongside the new anime season so readers can compare the two. The post covers chapters 92 to 94. The idea is to experience the story in multiple ways at the same time, reading the manga while watching the new episodes drop. Classic martial arts trope setup returning this season.
clips.text_en_b2: An anon is running a storytime thread covering the Ranma 1/2 manga alongside the brand-new anime season so readers can compare both versions directly. The current installment covers chapters 92 through 94, giving the community a chance to experience the classic martial arts setup in multiple formats at once. The poster mentions finishing his GI report before settling down with coffee to read, while also expressing a stronger urge to rewatch Gundam 00 from scratch.
clips.text_en_c1: An /a/ regular has launched a storytime thread revisiting the Ranma 1/2 manga in deliberate parallel with the freshly airing anime reboot, allowing readers to compare adaptation choices chapter by chapter. Current coverage spans chapters 92 through 94, with the poster cross-referencing paneling decisions, tonal shifts, and translation liberties against the televised counterpart. The premise offers a layered nostalgic experience for those who originally encountered the series through localized broadcasts in past decades. Discussion has predictably diverged into tangential territory, with several anons already confessing they would sooner commit to a full Gundam 00 rewatch than continue engaging with newer seasonal offerings.
clips.text_en_c2: An anonymous contributor on the anime board has inaugurated a synchronised storytime exercise, wherein the Ranma 1/2 manga is read in parallel with the freshly broadcast anime reboot, permitting attentive viewers to discern, chapter by episode, the precise calibrations of adaptation. The current instalment encompasses chapters 92 through 94, a stretch that aficionados recognise as pivotal to the martial arts tournament arc. The underlying premise is straightforward yet elegant: to inhabit a beloved narrative through multiple aesthetic registers simultaneously, savouring Rumiko Takahashi's panel choreography whilst the contemporary animation breathes new voice into familiar scenes. Having completed an unappetising geotechnical report earlier in the evening, our host now brews coffee and settles in. Separately, having revisited Mobile Suit Gundam 00, he confesses renewed enthusiasm for that older series.
clips.source_hint: /a/ storytime thread running Ranma 1/2 manga chapters with the new anime.
